questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis with indurated edges and a clean base. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged but non-tender. Dark field microscopy reveals spirochetes. What is the MOST appropriate treatment?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is caused by Treponema pallidum. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose is the treatment of choice. Doxycycline for 14 days is the alternative for penicillin-allergic patients. Dark field microscopy of the chancre exudate showing motile spirochetes confirms the diagnosis.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman presents with hypopigmented anaesthetic patches on her forearm. Slit skin smear is negative. Nerve biopsy shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells, lymphocytes, and no bacilli. What type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells in nerve biopsy. Lesions are few, well-defined, hypopigmented, anaesthetic, and SSS-negative (paucibacillary). Lepromatous leprosy shows foam cells (Virchow cells) packed with bacilli. BT shows ill-defined satellite granulomas. Indeterminate shows only non-specific lymphocytic infiltrate.

questions.q: A 45-year-old diabetic male develops painful erythematous plaques with peripheral vesiculation and central necrosis on his leg. The lesion spreads rapidly with foul smell. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in chains. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Necrotizing fasciitis type II is caused by Group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) — gram-positive cocci in chains. It presents with rapid necrosis, systemic toxicity, and high mortality. Type I is polymicrobial; type II is monomicrobial (GAS). Management requires emergency surgical debridement plus IV penicillin with clindamycin (to block toxin production).

questions.q: A 25-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 count 80 cells/μL) presents with multiple flesh-coloured dome-shaped papules with central umbilication on the face and trunk. The causative virus belongs to which family?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum virus (MCV) belongs to the Poxviridae family. In immunocompromised patients (CD4 <200), lesions are larger (giant molluscum), more numerous, and distributed on the face. Histology shows pathognomonic Henderson-Paterson (molluscum) bodies — eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions. Treatment: curettage, cryotherapy, or imiquimod; treat underlying immunodeficiency.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman develops tense bullae on normal-appearing skin of the lower abdomen and thighs. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents in the elderly with tense bullae on erythematous or normal skin, negative Nikolsky sign, and intense pruritus. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ. Target antigens are BP180 (BPAG2/type XVII collagen) and BP230 (BPAG1) at the hemidesmosome. Pemphigus vulgaris shows IgG in an intercellular pattern with positive Nikolsky sign.

questions.q: A 32-year-old male presents with annular erythematous plaques with central clearing and scaling at the advancing border on the inner thigh. KOH mount shows septate hyphae with arthrospores. The most appropriate topical antifungal is:
questions.exp: Tinea cruris is caused by dermatophytes (most commonly Trichophyton rubrum). Topical terbinafine 1% cream is the treatment of choice — it is fungicidal (inhibits squalene epoxidase in the ergosterol pathway). Nystatin and amphotericin B are effective only against Candida and are NOT effective against dermatophytes. Griseofulvin has no effective topical formulation.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with a butterfly-shaped facial rash, photosensitivity, and joint pains for 6 months. ANA is positive with elevated anti-dsDNA. Skin biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis. What is the expected DIF finding on lesional skin?
opts: Linear IgG and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction
Granular IgG, IgM, and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction
IgG in intercellular spaces of epidermis
questions.exp: The lupus band test (DIF on lesional skin in SLE) shows granular deposits of IgG, IgM, IgA, and C3 at the dermoepidermal junction due to immune complex deposition. On non-lesional sun-exposed skin, it is positive in 50-70% of SLE cases. Linear IgG is seen in bullous pemphigoid; granular IgA in dermal papillae is pathognomonic of dermatitis herpetiformis.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male smoker presents with a slowly enlarging pearly translucent nodule with rolled telangiectatic borders and a central ulcer on the nose for 2 years. Histology shows tumour islands with peripheral palisading and stromal retraction artefact. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nodular basal cell carcinoma (BCC) presents as a pearly papule/nodule with rolled borders, telangiectasia, and central ulceration ('rodent ulcer') on sun-exposed areas (nose most common). Histology shows basaloid tumour islands with peripheral nuclear palisading and peri-tumoral stromal retraction. SCC shows keratinisation (keratin pearls); keratoacanthoma grows rapidly with a keratin-filled crater.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with grouped vesicles on erythematous base on the genitals with burning pain and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. It is his first episode. The MOST appropriate treatment regimen is:
opts: Famciclovir 750 mg once daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Primary genital herpes (usually HSV-2) requires a longer treatment course than recurrent episodes. Acyclovir 400 mg TDS for 7-10 days is the standard regimen for first-episode genital herpes. Recurrent episodes use shorter courses (5 days). Valacyclovir 1g BD for 7-10 days or famciclovir 250 mg TDS for 7-10 days are also acceptable alternatives for first episodes.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT suddenly develops fever, tender erythematous nodular lesions over the body, iridocyclitis, and orchitis. Histology of the lesion shows neutrophilic infiltration and complement deposition. What is the immediate treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) is a Type 2 lepra reaction seen in BL/LL leprosy caused by immune complex deposition (Type III hypersensitivity). It presents with fever, tender erythematous nodules, and systemic involvement (iridocyclitis, orchitis, neuritis). Treatment: thalidomide 100-400 mg/day (drug of choice for males) or prednisolone. MDT must be CONTINUED. Type 1 reaction is treated with prednisolone only.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with a 15-year history of Raynaud's phenomenon, sclerodactyly, telangiectasias on the face and hands, and dysphagia. Which antibody is MOST specific for her condition?
questions.exp: This patient has CREST syndrome (Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) — the limited cutaneous form of systemic sclerosis (lcSSc). Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is highly specific for lcSSc/CREST (positive in 60-80%). Anti-Scl-70 is specific for diffuse cutaneous SSc (dcSSc) and carries worse prognosis (pulmonary fibrosis). Anti-Jo-1 is associated with antisynthetase syndrome in dermatomyositis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old farmer presents with a painless triad of subcutaneous swellings, multiple sinuses, and black granule discharge from the foot. X-ray shows bone destruction. What is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Eumycetoma (Madura foot) due to Madurella mycetomatis (most common in India) produces black granules. Actinomycetoma (Nocardia, Actinomyces — bacteria) produces white or yellow granules. Eumycetoma is treated with itraconazole ± surgical debridement; actinomycetoma with co-trimoxazole ± amikacin. Sporothrix schenckii causes lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis following thorn prick injuries.

questions.q: A 65-year-old man presents with intensely pruritic vesicular eruption on the extensor surfaces and buttocks. Small bowel biopsy reveals subtotal villous atrophy. DIF of perilesional skin shows granular IgA in dermal papillae. What is the FIRST-LINE treatment?
opts: Dapsone 100 mg/day plus strict gluten-free diet
Doxycycline 100 mg BD with nicotinamide 500 mg TDS
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is an IgA-mediated blistering disorder associated with celiac disease. DIF shows pathognomonic granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. The target antigen is epidermal transglutaminase (TG3). Treatment: dapsone provides rapid pruritus relief within 24-72 hours; strict lifelong gluten-free diet is the only treatment addressing the underlying cause. Unlike in BP, corticosteroids are NOT first-line in DH.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male presents with flesh-coloured exophytic warts on the penis and perineum. Acetowhitening test is positive. PCR confirms HPV. Which HPV types are responsible for anogenital condylomata acuminata?
questions.exp: Condyloma acuminata (anogenital warts) are caused by low-risk HPV types 6 and 11. High-risk types (HPV 16, 18, 31, 33) are associated with anogenital malignancies (cervical SCC, penile cancer). HPV 1 and 2 cause palmoplantar and common warts respectively; HPV 5 and 8 are associated with epidermodysplasia verruciformis (EV). Treatment options include podophyllotoxin, imiquimod, trichloroacetic acid, or ablative methods.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with symmetric proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules over the knuckles, and periungual erythema. What investigation is MOST diagnostic?
opts: Electromyography showing polyphasic motor unit potentials
Muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy with perimysial inflammation
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis (DM) diagnosis: the MOST diagnostic test is muscle biopsy showing perifascicular atrophy with perimysial and perivascular inflammation dominated by B cells and CD4+ T cells (complement-mediated microangiopathy). EMG shows myopathic pattern but is non-specific. CK is elevated but not diagnostic. Anti-Jo-1 is positive in only 20-30% (antisynthetase syndrome). Heliotrope rash and Gottron's papules are pathognomonic skin signs.

questions.q: A woodcutter presents with a painless warty plaque on the dorsum of his right hand, slowly enlarging over 3 years. Biopsy shows well-differentiated squamous cells with keratin pearl formation, invading the dermis. No lymph node enlargement. Most appropriate management?
opts: Wide local excision with 1 cm margins
questions.exp: This is a low-risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Wide local excision with 1 cm margins is standard for low-risk SCC (<2 cm, well-differentiated, no perineural invasion, not on face). Mohs surgery is preferred for high-risk SCC, recurrent lesions, or cosmetically sensitive locations. Topical 5-FU is for actinic keratosis and SCC in situ (Bowen's disease), not invasive SCC.

questions.q: A patient suspected of having allergic contact dermatitis to hair dye undergoes patch testing. Which allergen is used to test for hair dye allergy in the European Baseline Series?
questions.exp: p-Phenylenediamine (PPD) at 1% in petrolatum is the standard patch test allergen for oxidative hair dye allergy. PPD cross-reacts with para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) in sunscreens, benzocaine (local anaesthetic), sulfonamides, and azo dyes. Nickel sulfate is the most common contact allergen overall. Potassium dichromate is the allergen for cement/leather dermatitis. Formaldehyde is found in cosmetics, clothing, and resins.

questions.q: A neonate presents at birth with generalised blistering affecting over 30% of BSA. Electron microscopy of the biopsy shows cleavage within the lamina lucida of the basement membrane zone. Which gene mutation is MOST likely responsible?
opts: LAMA3, LAMB3, or LAMC2 (laminin-332) or COL17A1
questions.exp: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa (JEB) shows cleavage within the lamina lucida on EM. The most common mutations are in LAMA3, LAMB3, LAMC2 (encoding laminin-332 subunits) or COL17A1 (encoding type XVII collagen/BP180). Herlitz JEB (LAMA3/LAMB3/LAMC2 mutations) is the most severe and often lethal. EBS (intraepidermal cleavage) is due to KRT5/KRT14 mutations; DEB (sublamina densa) is due to COL7A1 mutations.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for SLE develops painless visual field defects (bull's eye maculopathy). Hydroxychloroquine exerts its therapeutic effect by which mechanism?
opts: Lysosomal accumulation, raising pH and blocking TLR-7 and TLR-9 signalling
Calcineurin inhibition and blockade of IL-2 transcription
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) is a lysosomotropic weak base that accumulates in acidic organelles, raises their pH, and inhibits antigen presentation and endosomal Toll-like receptor (TLR-7, TLR-9) signalling, thereby reducing type I interferon production. Its major toxicity is irreversible retinopathy (bull's eye maculopathy at the fovea), requiring baseline ophthalmology and annual screening after 5 years of use. Leflunomide inhibits DHODH; tacrolimus inhibits calcineurin.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with hypopigmented macules on the trunk for 6 months. Wood's lamp examination shows golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH mount shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia species (M. globosa, M. restricta). The organism produces pteridines causing golden-yellow fluorescence on Wood's lamp. KOH mount shows characteristic 'spaghetti and meatballs' (short curved hyphae + round spores). Azelaic acid produced by the organism inhibits tyrosinase causing hypopigmentation. Treatment: topical selenium sulfide, ketoconazole shampoo, or oral itraconazole/fluconazole.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man presents with flaccid bullae involving the oral mucosa and trunk for 3 months. Nikolsky sign is positive. Histology shows suprabasal acantholysis with 'tombstone' appearance of basal cells. Which antibody mediates this disease?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (PV) is caused by IgG antibodies against desmoglein 3 (Dsg3), a desmosomal cadherin crucial for cell-cell adhesion in the spinous layer. This causes suprabasal acantholysis. Oral involvement (most common initial site) corresponds to anti-Dsg3 alone; skin involvement requires anti-Dsg1 in addition. Anti-Dsg1 alone causes pemphigus foliaceus (no oral involvement). Anti-envoplakin is for paraneoplastic pemphigus.

questions.q: A 7-year-old child presents with ash-leaf shaped hypopigmented macules, shagreen patches, periungual fibromas, and cortical tubers on MRI brain. What is the inheritance pattern and causative genes?
opts: X-linked recessive; NF1 and NF2 genes
questions.exp: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is an autosomal dominant neurocutaneous syndrome caused by loss-of-function mutations in TSC1 (chromosome 9q34, hamartin) or TSC2 (chromosome 16p13, tuberin). These proteins form a complex inhibiting mTORC1. Cutaneous features: ash-leaf macules (earliest sign), facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum), shagreen patches, periungual fibromas, and confetti macules. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) treat subependymal giant-cell astrocytomas and pulmonary LAM.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery, horizontal (tangential/en face) frozen sections are used. What is the primary advantage over standard vertical (bread-loaf) sections in conventional excision?
opts: Better assessment of tumour depth of invasion
Faster processing time allowing same-day results
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS) uses horizontal en-face frozen sections that allow examination of 100% of the peripheral and deep surgical margins simultaneously (conventional bread-loaf sections sample only ~1-2% of margins). This maximises tumour clearance while conserving maximum normal tissue. Indications: high-risk BCCs/SCCs, tumours on the H-zone of the face, recurrent tumours, and tumours with ill-defined borders or perineural invasion.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with photosensitivity and burning on sun-exposed skin. Her urine turns pink-red in sunlight and shows coral-pink fluorescence under Wood's lamp. She has a history of alcohol use. What enzyme deficiency underlies this condition?
questions.exp: Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT) is caused by deficiency of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase (UROD), leading to accumulation of uroporphyrins in urine. Urine shows coral-pink fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Clinical features: photosensitivity, skin fragility on dorsa of hands, blistering, milia, hypertrichosis, and hyperpigmentation. Precipitants: alcohol, iron, oestrogens, hepatitis C. Treatment: phlebotomy (to reduce iron load) or low-dose hydroxychloroquine.

questions.q: A 16-year-old girl presents since infancy with café-au-lait spots with irregular 'coast of Maine' borders, polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, and precocious puberty. The underlying molecular defect is:
opts: Somatic activating mutation in GNAS gene (Gs-alpha protein)
Germline loss-of-function mutation in PTEN gene
questions.exp: McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is caused by a somatic (postzygotic mosaic) activating mutation in the GNAS1 gene encoding the Gs-alpha subunit of G-proteins. This leads to constitutive cAMP production, causing the triad: polyostotic fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots with irregular 'coast of Maine' borders, and autonomous endocrine hyperfunction (precocious puberty most common). NF1 café-au-lait spots have smooth 'coast of California' borders. STK11 mutation causes Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man on methotrexate for psoriasis develops painful oral ulcers and macrocytic anaemia. Methotrexate causes these adverse effects by inhibiting which enzyme?
questions.exp: Methotrexate (MTX) competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), preventing conversion of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate. This depletes the folate pool needed for thymidylate and purine synthesis, inhibiting DNA replication in rapidly proliferating cells (keratinocytes, bone marrow). Folic acid supplementation reduces toxicity (mucositis, megaloblastic anaemia) without significantly reducing anti-psoriatic efficacy. Leflunomide inhibits DHODH; mycophenolate inhibits IMPDH.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male presents with reticulate hyperpigmentation on the trunk, nail dystrophy, and white oral plaques since young adulthood. His son has similar features and his blood counts show pancytopenia. The X-linked recessive form of this condition is due to mutation in which gene?
questions.exp: Dyskeratosis congenita (DC) is characterised by the mucocutaneous triad: reticulate hyperpigmentation, nail dystrophy, and oral leukoplakia, plus bone marrow failure, pulmonary fibrosis, and increased risk of malignancy. It is a telomere biology disorder. The X-linked recessive form (Zinsser-Engman-Cole syndrome) is caused by mutations in DKC1 (encoding dyskerin, which is part of the H/ACA telomerase complex). Other forms involve TERC, TERT, TINF2, etc.

questions.q: A patient with severe plaque psoriasis is started on a biologic. The drug specifically neutralises IL-17A. Which of the following agents targets IL-17A exclusively?
questions.exp: Secukinumab and ixekizumab both specifically target IL-17A. Bimekizumab targets both IL-17A and IL-17F, providing broader IL-17 blockade. Ustekinumab targets the p40 subunit common to IL-12 and IL-23. Risankizumab, guselkumab, and tildrakizumab target the p19 subunit of IL-23. The IL-17A/IL-17RA axis is central to psoriasis pathogenesis and anti-IL-17 biologics show among the highest PASI 90/100 response rates.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with intensely pruritic burrows in the web spaces, wrists, and periareolar region. Several hostel roommates have similar nocturnal pruritus. Dermoscopy shows the 'delta-wing jet with contrail' sign. What is the most appropriate treatment for the entire household?
opts: Topical lindane 1% applied to the whole body once
Topical permethrin 5% cream applied neck to toes, left 8-12 hours, repeated after 1 week
Oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg single dose only
Topical benzyl benzoate 25% applied to the face and body for 3 days
questions.exp: Scabies is caused by Sarcoptes scabiei var. hominis. Permethrin 5% cream is the treatment of choice — applied from neck to toes, left for 8-12 hours, then washed off, repeated after 7 days. It is safe in pregnancy (category B) and children >2 months. ALL household contacts and sexual partners must be treated simultaneously. Oral ivermectin is preferred for crusted/Norwegian scabies. Lindane is neurotoxic and no longer recommended. Permethrin also treats clothing and bedding (wash at 60°C).

questions.q: A 35-year-old fishmonger presents with a violaceous, well-demarcated, spreading cellulitis on the right index finger, 3 weeks after handling raw fish. There is no systemic upset. The causative organism is a gram-positive rod. What is this condition?
questions.exp: Erysipeloid of Rosenbach is an occupational infection of fishmongers, butchers, and veterinarians caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae (gram-positive rod). It presents as a slowly spreading, violaceous, well-demarcated cellulitis on fingers/hands without systemic symptoms. There are three forms: localised cutaneous (most common), diffuse cutaneous, and septicaemic. Treatment: penicillin or amoxicillin (naturally resistant to vancomycin). Fish tank granuloma (M. marinum) shows sporotrichoid nodular lymphangitis.
